headline: Discussed a possible local Overdose Fatality Review Committee; group agreed to review evidence-based practices for it.
summary: Partners reported that suspected overdose trends are approximately 7% lower than last year. The group discussed a possible Overdose Fatality Review Committee in Nashua and recommended that the City not facilitate waiving Right-to-Know requirements.
decisions: Agreed to review evidence-based practices to determine how an Overdose Fatality Review Committee could be implemented locally.
Recommended that the City not facilitate the waiver of Right-to-Know requirements for the proposed committee.

decision_evidence.quote: The group agreed that evidence-based practices should be reviewed to determine how an OFRC could be implemented locally and to learn from approaches used in other communities.
One concern is the ability to waive Right-to-Know requirements. It is recommended that this not be facilitated by the City.

decision_titles: Review of evidence-based practices for an Overdose Fatality Review Committee
City not facilitating waiver of Right-to-Know requirements

1 | P a g e  
 
City of Nashua 
Division of Public Health and Community Services 
 
Mayor’s Task Force on Substance Misuse Meeting 
 
Tuesday, 10/20/2026 
9:30 – 11 a.m. 
Facilitator: Bobbie Bagley, Director DPHCS         Location: City Hall Auditorium, 3rd Floor 
Minutes 
 Partner Updates  
United Way  
• The fourth annual karaoke event will be held at the Nashua Center for the 
Arts. The event will feature performances and a jury-judged competition. 
Approximately 600 seats are available, with discounted tickets offered. 
Registration is available on the United Way website. 
NH National Guard  
• Drug Take Back Day is scheduled for October 24 and 26. 
Nashua Prevention Coalition:  
• Red Ribbon Week will take place October 28–29. 
• Students participating in after-school activities will take part in drug-free 
activities on October 26. Five schools will take part, with visits and 
photographs planned at each school. 
Nashua Regional Planning Commission: 
• Reported receiving 64 transportation assistance requests to date, including 
transportation to Manchester and specialized rides to other locations. 
• Surplus bicycles are available for individuals in recovery. The program is 
expanding, and additional space is needed. Please share information about 
potential larger spaces with the group. City Bike Coop is open to individuals 
seeking volunteer hours. 
Doorways 
• A satellite location is expected to open soon. Information will be included in 
the newsletter. 
AMR Data 
Overdose Trends 
• Suspected overdose trends reported by AMR are approximately 7% lower than 
last year, continuing a record-low trend and five consecutive years of decline. 
• An additional 13% decrease was reported in another measure. Further 
demographic information was discussed. 
• A total of 40 overdoses were reported: 10 in Nashua and 30 in Manchester. 
Three occurred in Nashua and four in Manchester during the reporting period 
discussed. 
• Year-to-date data for Nashua and Manchester indicates the lowest annual 
overdose totals in 11 years. 
• Reported public Narcan use increased by 35% in Manchester and 37% in
2 | P a g e  
 
Nashua. 
Police Department Data 
• Opioid-related overdose data reviewed for the past five years. 
• In September 2025, eight overdoses were reported, compared with seven in 
September 2026. 
• A question was raised about obtaining overdose data from other towns in the 
Nashua region. Current data collection is limited to the Nashua Police 
Department. Collecting data from all 13 towns would provide a more 
complete regional picture. The Planning Commission is not currently collecting 
this information, although smaller towns also experience overdose-related 
issues. 
• One additional overdose-related death was reported compared with 
September 2025. 
SSANA Update 
• A comparison of SSANA transactions in 2025 and 2026 was presented. Please 
refer to the slides for detailed information. 
• The group discussed the challenges associated with moving services from the 
library to the REVIVE parking lot. 
• Drug use in the library restrooms resulted in significant damage, discarded 
needles, and other drug-related paraphernalia. 
• Participation at REVIVE has decreased. Additional education and outreach are 
needed to help participants understand expectations and encourage 
accountability. 
• The REVIVE parking lot is too small to accommodate the service. 
Housing Services 
Officer Update 
• A press release was issued regarding the Resource Center initiative. October 5 
marked the first day of operations. A steady stream of individuals has been 
accessing services. Part-time staff have been hired.  
• The Board of Aldermen (BOA) has established a gap analysis committee. 
• The warming station is scheduled to open on November 16. 
Overdose Fatality 
Review Committee 
(OFRC) Discussion 
 
• Although overdose numbers are trending downward, overdose-related deaths 
continue to occur. 
• The group discussed establishing an Overdose Fatality Review Committee 
(OFRC) in Nashua. 
• One concern is the ability to waive Right-to-Know requirements. It is 
recommended that this not be facilitated by the City.    
• If information is requested under the Right-to-Know law, the city may be 
required to provide it. 
• A partner organization may be willing to serve as the host for the committee. 
• Manchester's current process involves the Police Department, Fire 
Department, and Public Health. Police officers and social workers conduct 
follow-up investigations at individuals' homes. 
• The group discussed how the state reviews overdose deaths, including the 
discussion of personal circumstances. Names and identifying details are
3 | P a g e  
 
redacted. 
• The group agreed that evidence-based practices should be reviewed to 
determine how an OFRC could be implemented locally and to learn from 
approaches used in other communities. 
• Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) are an important component of 
prevention. The report should emphasize early intervention, continued 
engagement, and ensuring that individuals do not fall through the cracks. 
• The group discussed reaching out to Manchester to learn more about its 
approach and opportunities for additional funding to expand services to all 
schools. 
• The Mayor of Manchester has established a Child Care Commission to develop 
strategies to support families. A report is expected in November. 
• Real-time data, including overdose hot spots, are also available. 
Opioid Abatement 
Trust Fund  
• Funds have not yet been transferred to the Opioid Trust Fund account. 
Requests from organizations that have applied for grants will move forward 
for review once the funds are transferred. The Mayor's Office reviews the 
applications for project approval. 
 
   
Next Meeting October 20, 2026
